learner_notice: Commit one response before feedback appears. Exit misses may release one bounded function-specific repair and one fresh re-entry.

items.title: Starting check: follow the route
items.prompt: Which sequence follows ingested material through the alimentary canal without reversing two adjacent compartments?
options: Mouth → stomach → esophagus → small intestine → large intestine
Mouth → esophagus → stomach → small intestine → large intestine
Mouth → esophagus → small intestine → stomach → large intestine
Mouth → stomach → small intestine → esophagus → large intestine
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Guided practice: combine the clues
items.prompt: A compartment stores a meal, mixes it with muscular contractions, maintains a strongly acidic lumen, and begins substantial protein digestion. Which compartment is described?
options: Large intestine
Esophagus
Small intestine
Stomach
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Less help: protect the stomach wall
items.prompt: Which local feature most directly limits self-injury while the stomach lumen remains strongly acidic?
options: A mucus-and-bicarbonate barrier at the epithelium
A permanently neutral stomach lumen
A villus network that exports absorbed lipids
A rectal sphincter that delays elimination
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: On your own: classify the movement
items.prompt: A ring of smooth muscle contracts behind a bolus while the segment ahead relaxes. What is the primary immediate function of this pattern?
options: Neutralize acid entering the small intestine
Hydrolyze peptide bonds in the bolus
Propel luminal contents along the tract
Absorb monosaccharides into capillaries
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Near exit: locate the processing site
items.prompt: Acidic chyme enters a highly folded compartment where bicarbonate raises pH, enzymes continue digestion, and most nutrient absorption occurs. Which compartment is it?
options: Stomach
Small intestine
Large intestine
Rectum
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Changed-task exit: isolate a motility defect
items.prompt: A drug selectively suppresses coordinated smooth-muscle waves in the small intestine but leaves bicarbonate and digestive-enzyme secretion intact. Which change should occur first?
options: Protein hydrolysis stops because all enzymes disappear
The gastric mucus barrier immediately dissolves
Bile can no longer emulsify lipids chemically
Propulsion and mixing of intestinal contents slow
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Repair: match every clue
items.prompt: A downstream compartment recovers water from remaining material and supports a dense microbial community. Which compartment fits both clues?
options: Large intestine
Stomach
Esophagus
Rectum
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: locate final storage
items.prompt: After most water has been recovered, material is held temporarily immediately before defecation. Which compartment performs this storage role?
options: Small intestine
Large intestine
Rectum
Stomach
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Repair: hold secretions constant
items.prompt: If esophageal peristaltic waves fail while swallowing and gastric secretion remain intact, which direct consequence is most likely?
options: Small-intestinal villi lose surface area
Bolus transport toward the stomach slows
The liver stops producing bile
The large intestine can no longer host flora
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: predict a new movement loss
items.prompt: Stomach acid and protein-digesting enzymes remain normal, but gastric muscular churning is selectively lost. Which outcome is most direct?
options: The esophagus reverses the route of a swallowed bolus
All chemical protein digestion becomes impossible
Rectal storage ends immediately
Mechanical mixing of the meal with gastric secretions decreases
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Starting check: find the bile source
items.prompt: Which organ produces bile before that secretion is stored or delivered to the small intestine?
options: Gallbladder
Pancreas
Liver
Large intestine
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Guided practice: store the secretion
items.prompt: Between meals, which structure stores and concentrates liver-produced bile for later release?
options: Gallbladder
Pancreatic islet
Stomach lumen
Hepatic portal vein
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Less help: classify bile action
items.prompt: What is the most direct digestive action of bile after it reaches the small intestine?
options: Hydrolyze peptide bonds into amino acids
Convert glucose directly into glycogen in muscle
Neutralize every acid molecule by enzymatic cleavage
Disperse large lipid droplets into smaller droplets
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: On your own: choose the pancreatic route
items.prompt: A pancreatic product travels through a duct and acts in the small-intestinal lumen. Which product best fits that route?
options: Insulin regulating glucose uptake in muscle
A digestive protease precursor released toward the intestine
Glucagon signaling the liver through circulation
A liver enzyme retained inside a hepatocyte
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Near exit: trace the bile chain
items.prompt: Which chain correctly connects bile production, storage, destination, and immediate digestive action?
options: Gallbladder production → liver storage → stomach delivery → protein hydrolysis
Pancreas production → liver storage → blood delivery → glucose uptake
Liver production → gallbladder storage → small-intestinal delivery → lipid emulsification
Liver production → pancreatic storage → colon delivery → peptide cleavage
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Changed-task exit: separate pancreatic routes
items.prompt: A stone blocks the pancreatic duct, but endocrine pancreatic cells remain viable and well supplied with blood. Which paired outcome is most likely first?
options: Fewer digestive enzymes reach the intestine while hormone release to blood can remain
Insulin cannot enter blood while intestinal enzyme delivery remains normal
Bile production stops while pancreatic bicarbonate delivery increases
Liver detoxification stops while gallbladder storage becomes endocrine
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Repair: rebuild the bile chain
items.prompt: Which statement assigns bile production and storage to the correct two structures?
options: The gallbladder produces bile, and the liver stores it
The pancreas produces bile, and the stomach stores it
The small intestine produces bile, and the colon stores it
The liver produces bile, and the gallbladder stores it
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: reason without a reservoir
items.prompt: After gallbladder removal, the liver and bile ducts remain functional. Which statement is most accurate?
options: Bile production ends because the storage organ was removed
Bile still reaches the intestine, but gallbladder storage is lost
Pancreatic islets begin producing replacement bile
The large intestine becomes the new bile reservoir
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Repair: identify the route
items.prompt: Which pancreatic output normally enters blood rather than a duct leading to the small intestine?
options: A protease precursor
Bicarbonate-rich pancreatic fluid
Insulin
A lipid-digesting pancreatic enzyme
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: move the defect to endocrine cells
items.prompt: Pancreatic beta cells are selectively damaged, but acinar cells and the pancreatic duct remain functional. Which paired effect is most direct?
options: Insulin regulation declines while digestive-enzyme delivery can remain
Bile synthesis declines while intestinal water absorption remains
Digestive enzymes disappear while insulin secretion remains normal
Gallbladder storage ends while glucagon becomes a duct enzyme
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Starting check: enlarge the interface
items.prompt: Which structural feature most directly increases small-intestinal absorptive surface without requiring a longer tube?
options: A thicker serosal layer around the intestine
A single smooth epithelial sheet without projections
A wider rectal storage chamber
Villi and microvilli projecting toward the lumen
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Guided practice: adjust the pH
items.prompt: Acidic chyme enters the duodenum from the stomach. Which immediate change best supports the activity of many intestinal and pancreatic enzymes?
options: Add more gastric acid to keep the lumen strongly acidic
Deliver bicarbonate to raise the luminal pH
Remove all water from the intestinal lumen
Close every pancreatic and biliary duct
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Less help: locate the enzyme
items.prompt: An enzyme is anchored to the apical membrane of a small-intestinal epithelial cell and acts on a nutrient immediately before uptake. Where does it act?
options: Inside the gallbladder reservoir
Within the large-intestinal microbial community
At the brush border facing the intestinal lumen
Inside a pancreatic endocrine cell before blood release
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: On your own: follow the remaining water
items.prompt: After most nutrients have been absorbed, which downstream compartment recovers additional water and supports abundant microbial flora?
options: Large intestine
Esophagus
Stomach
Pancreatic duct
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Near exit: change the villus surface
items.prompt: A treatment flattens small-intestinal villi but leaves nutrient digestion and luminal concentration unchanged. Which direct effect is most likely?
options: Bile production by the liver immediately stops
Gastric churning becomes the main absorption route
Rectal storage capacity increases enough to restore uptake
The rate of nutrient absorption across the epithelium decreases
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Changed-task exit: isolate local control
items.prompt: A toxin blocks a local enteric sensory-to-motor circuit in one intestinal segment. Circulating digestive hormones and their receptors remain functional. Which effect is most direct?
options: All endocrine signaling to every digestive organ stops
Local coordination of motility and secretion is impaired in that segment
Villi instantly disappear from the entire small intestine
The liver can no longer transform any absorbed compound
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Repair: hold the other variables constant
items.prompt: Two intestinal segments receive the same nutrient concentration and blood flow. Segment A has twice the functional epithelial surface area of segment B. What should increase most directly in A?
options: The acidity of gastric juice upstream
The number of rectal storage events
The potential rate of nutrient absorption
The need for every pancreatic enzyme to enter blood
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: change microvilli
items.prompt: A mutation shortens epithelial microvilli while leaving villus number, digestion, and perfusion unchanged. Which outcome is expected?
options: Lower absorptive capacity from reduced apical surface area
Higher absorption because a smoother surface always mixes faster
Complete loss of large-intestinal flora
Immediate overproduction of bile by the gallbladder
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Repair: identify the controller route
items.prompt: Which observation most specifically indicates endocrine rather than local enteric control of a digestive target?
options: Stretch activates nearby sensory neurons and a short local motor loop
A bolus is propelled by contraction behind it and relaxation ahead
A brush-border enzyme acts beside the epithelial membrane
A messenger travels in blood and binds receptors on the pancreas
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: move the defect to a hormone target
items.prompt: A gallbladder loses receptors for a circulating digestive hormone, but its local enteric innervation remains intact. Which effect is most direct?
options: Every local intestinal reflex disappears
Hormone-triggered gallbladder contraction is reduced
Villus surface area doubles throughout the intestine
The pancreas becomes unable to release any enzyme through its duct
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.
